newsitem.title: FRANCE: Valeo says can afford large acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Valeo says can afford large acquisitions.

text.p: Car parts manufacturer Valeo has the financial means to make large acquisitions, chairman Noel Goutard said in an interview with daily Le Figaro.
"We do not rule out large acquisitions, our financial situation allows it," Goutard said.
He also said that in coming years the group would continue to develop in Europe, North and South America but would also target Asia and central Europe.
"Within five years we want to generate over half of our sales outside Europe, 25 percent in North America and 25 percent in South America, Asia and central Europe," he said.
This would be achieved through the construction of new plants, joint-ventures with local partners and acquisitions, he said.

Goutard also said that despite fierce price competition, Valeo would strive to improve profit margins. He said the group will invest two billion francs ($330.6 million) in research and development and three billion francs in its industrial operations in 1997.
He reiterated that Valeo sought to generate over 40 billion francs in sales by the year 2000.
"We have set an annual growth target of at least 10 percent to generate sales of over 40 billion francs in the year 2000," he said.
